args.text: Glaze failures (day 37): (1) tree_glaze (viridian 1.5/raw umber 1.5/ultramarine .8/yellow ochre .5, medium 0.55) laid with hand='glaze' coverage 0.55 over dry tree line: glaze hand's 120-300-unit strokes formed huge dark TEAL diagonal slabs across the trees — viridian at that share is far too chromatic/dark even 'transparent', and long glaze strokes do not make a uniform tone at low coverage. (2) Sky veil (glaze hand, medium 0.35 sky piles, mask = original sky_m minus canopy) SLICED the taller tree crowns along sky_m's old bottom edge (crowns now rise above it) leaving a straight pale band and frosty white crown tops; also left white triangular 'teeth' of glow between oak canopy lobes. Rag rescue (rag 55, dip .3, .62 pressure, 2 passes over y312-464) lifted most teal leaving scratch traces. RULES going forward (hypotheses from these trials): never use original sky_m as a mask again — its bottom edge no longer matches the tree silhouette; any sky pass must end at the CURRENT tree/canopy silhouette. Glazes for toning must be tested for chroma and laid at higher coverage with shorter tools than the default glaze hand, or not used. Final fix for trees: repaint the whole tree line in ONE body pass (after veil remnants dry) with tree_lit capped ~0.25 at tops (frost came from lit weight up to 0.7 at y330 in tree_m3 pass), and raise distant humps at x750-950 to y~315 to fill the white teeth under the oak with mid-green distant foliage.

        {storm_mid,  function(x,y) return clamp(0.25 + y/250*0.75, 0.1, 1.1) end},
        {glow,       function(x,y) return clamp(((y-140)/115)^2 * (0.3 + (x-480)/520*0.6), 0.0, 0.95) end}}})
-- B. canopy from a newly drawn irregular silhouette, over wet sky
canopy_m4 = poly({{745,0},{1000,0},{1000,300},{968,278},{940,318},{905,282},{872,322},{838,272},{800,300},{772,252},{730,268},{718,222},{682,214},{700,166},{664,140},{692,96},{708,58},{724,24}}, true)
